_comments: ContractNumber is SERVER-ASSIGNED, so the API must not treat it as a field the user supplies.
THE PROBLEM. The column is NOT NULL and ContractEntityServer.Save() mints it from
seq_ContractNumber on insert - but MJ's EntityField.Validate() refuses a NOT NULL field whose value
is null, and it runs in the BROWSER, before the server ever sees the record. So every create failed
with 'Contract Number cannot be null' and the number had to be typed by hand.
WHY AllowUpdateAPI = false IS THE LEVER. The validator's guard is
`if (!ef.ReadOnly && !ef.SkipValidation)`, and both of those are DERIVED:
ReadOnly       = !AllowUpdateAPI || IsPrimaryKey || IsSpecialDateField
SkipValidation = IsSpecialDateField || IsPrimaryKey || AutoIncrement || IsVirtual || ReadOnly
So clearing AllowUpdateAPI makes the field ReadOnly, which makes SkipValidation true, which skips
the null check entirely. It is also semantically honest: the number is minted by the server and was
never meant to be written through the API.
WHAT IT COSTS. Hand-typed contract numbers are gone from the ordinary form path. That is accepted
(Marcelo, 2026-08-21). If manual entry is wanted later it should be a deliberate 'override number'
affordance, not a default form field - and that is where the ^CTR-\d+$ reserved-pattern guard in
ContractEntity belongs.
WHAT WE TRIED FIRST, so it is not retried. A DB DEFAULT on the column would also satisfy the
validator (MJ treats a defaulted NOT NULL column as legal-when-null on a NEW record) - but CodeGen
string-quotes an EXPRESSION default into the generated create procedure, which then fails to compile
and leaves spCreateContract DROPPED. Filed as MJ#4000; added and reverted in V202608211000/1100.
IncludeInGeneratedForm: false was also considered and is purely presentational - it hides the red
box and does nothing about the save error.
⚠ REVERTED TO TRUE, 2026-08-21. AllowUpdateAPI = false DID silence the validator, and then broke
creation a different way: a ReadOnly field is OMITTED FROM THE INSERT PAYLOAD, so spCreateContract
failed with "expects parameter '@ContractNumber', which was not supplied". The server mints the
number inside Save(), but the generated CRUD call never carries it.
So BOTH available workarounds are dead ends, and that is the real finding:
· a DB DEFAULT breaks CodeGen (it string-quotes an expression default; MJ#4000)
· AllowUpdateAPI = false excludes the column from the insert (this)
There is currently no supported way to model a server-minted NOT NULL column. MJ#4001.

_comment: DisplayName 'Renewal Notice (Days)' (issue #28 item 6). UNLIKE the CompanyID case, this is a
real change: CodeGen derives 'Renewal Notice Days' -- it strips a trailing 'ID' from an FK but
does not bracket a unit -- and the parenthesised form is what the form's own label uses. The
field is one of a confusable pair with CancellationWindowDays ('notice we owe' vs 'notice we
are owed'), so a grid heading that reads differently from the form is a real cost.
Verified against the database before adding: the column held 'Renewal Notice Days'.
